s0001.literal: Jiang Zong, styled Zongchi, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang, tenth-generation descendant of Jin Regular Attendant of the Scattered Cavalry Tong.
s0001.idiomatic: Jiang Zong, styled Zongchi, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery, a tenth-generation descendant of Jin's regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, Jiang Tong.

s0002.literal: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan was Song Left Grand Master of the Palace, Grandee Opening the Mansion with Ceremonial Parity to the Three Offices, the loyal and simple Duke.
s0002.idiomatic: His fifth-generation ancestor Zhan had been Song's left grand master of the palace and a grandee opening the mansion with ceremonial parity to the three offices, posthumously titled the loyal and simple duke.

s0003.literal: His grandfather Qian was Liang Minister of the Household, famed in his generation.
s0003.idiomatic: His grandfather Qian had been Liang's minister of the household and was famed in his generation.

s0004.literal: His father Gou was the commandery's welcoming chief clerk; in youth he observed mourning for his father and died from grief-induced injury to his body—recorded in the Biography of Filial Conduct in the Book of Liang.
s0004.idiomatic: His father Gou had been the commandery's welcoming chief clerk; in youth he observed mourning for his father and died from grief-induced injury to his body, as recorded in the Biography of Filial Conduct in the Book of Liang.

s0005.literal: Zong was orphaned at seven and lived with his mother's family.
s0005.idiomatic: Zong was orphaned at seven and lived with his mother's family.

s0006.literal: As a child he was clever and keen, with utmost nature.
s0006.idiomatic: As a child he was clever and keen, with an utmost nature.

s0007.literal: His uncle, Marquis Pingguang of Wu, Xiao Mei, Editorial footnote marker 1. bore a weighty name in his day and cherished Zong especially. He once told Zong: "Your conduct is wholly unlike others', your spirit striking and elevated; when you are famous hereafter, you will stand above me.
s0007.idiomatic: His uncle, the Marquis of Pingguang in Wu, Xiao Mei, [1] bore a weighty name in his day and cherished Zong especially. He once told Zong, "Your conduct is wholly unlike others', your spirit striking and elevated; when you are famous hereafter, you will stand above me.

s0008.literal: " When grown he studied diligently and had literary grace. The family held several thousand volumes of imperial grants; Zong read day and night without ever laying them down.
s0008.idiomatic: " When grown he studied diligently and had literary grace. The family held several thousand volumes of imperial grants; Zong read day and night without ever laying them down.

s0009.literal: At eighteen he was first appointed law-cadet in the establishment of the All-Courtesy Prince of Wuling.
s0009.idiomatic: At eighteen he was first appointed law-cadet in the establishment of the All-Courtesy Prince of Wuling.

s0010.literal: When Central Authority General and Governor of Danyang He Jingrong opened his mansion and appointed staff clerks, all were filled with noble scions; Zong was furthermore made chief clerk in Jingrong's establishment.
s0010.idiomatic: When central authority general and governor of Danyang He Jingrong opened his mansion and appointed staff clerks, all posts were filled with noble scions; Zong was furthermore made chief clerk in Jingrong's establishment.

s0011.literal: Promoted to Master of Writing Palace Retainer.
s0011.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace retainer in the Masters of Writing.

s0012.literal: When Liang's Emperor Wu had just finished compiling the Correct Language, he composed a poem expressing his feelings; Zong took part in the composition. The Emperor read Zong's poem and lowered his voice in deep admiration.
s0012.idiomatic: When Liang's Emperor Wu had just finished compiling the Correct Language, he composed a poem expressing his feelings; Zong took part in the composition. The emperor read Zong's poem and lowered his voice in deep admiration.

s0013.literal: He was then transferred to gentleman-attendant.
s0013.idiomatic: He was then transferred to gentleman-attendant.

s0014.literal: Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, Revenue Commissioner Wang Yun of Langya, and Discipline Commissioner Liu Zhiliao of Nanyang were all men of eminent talent and great learning. Zong at the time was young and already famed; Zuan and the rest warmly esteemed him, and they formed friendships across the generations.
s0014.idiomatic: Vice director of the masters of writing Zhang Zuan of Fanyang, revenue commissioner Wang Yun of Langya, and discipline commissioner Liu Zhiliao of Nanyang were all men of eminent talent and great learning. Zong at the time was young and already famed; Zuan and the rest warmly esteemed him, and they formed friendships across the generations.

s0015.literal: Liu Zhiliao's poem in reply to Zong, in summary: "You occupy a lofty rank and receive honored ritual; your office adjoins where I dwell.
s0015.idiomatic: Liu Zhiliao's poem in reply to Zong, in summary: "You occupy a lofty rank and receive honored ritual; your office adjoins where I dwell.

s0016.literal: I dread to hear the dawn outrider's cry; each morning I fear the blazing light.
s0016.idiomatic: I dread to hear the dawn outrider's cry; each morning I fear the blazing light.

s0017.literal: High talk whose meaning is not exhausted, meetings face to face whose appreciation has no end.
s0017.idiomatic: High talk whose meaning is not exhausted, meetings face to face whose appreciation has no end.

s0018.literal: We probe what is urgent and roam together; on rest days we forget to withdraw and eat.
s0018.idiomatic: We probe what is urgent and roam together; on rest days we forget to withdraw and eat.

s0019.literal: How could we wear away vulgar grudges? You deigned to set your feet in view and see my face.
s0019.idiomatic: How could we wear away vulgar grudges? You deigned to set your feet in view and see my face.

s0020.literal: Above and below, thousands of years—we buck and spill the feelings in our breast."
s0020.idiomatic: Above and below, thousands of years—we buck and spill the feelings in our breast."

s0021.literal: Such was the esteem in which men of the age held him.
s0021.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which men of the age held him.

s0022.literal: Promoted to groom of the heir apparent; then sent out as magistrate of Lin'an, returned as records clerk with limited commission in the Central Army Prince of Xuancheng's establishment, transferred to attendant of the heir apparent.
s0022.idiomatic: He was promoted to groom of the heir apparent; then sent out as magistrate of Lin'an, returned as records clerk with limited commission in the central army Prince of Xuancheng's establishment, and transferred to attendant of the heir apparent.

s0023.literal: When friendship was restored with Wei, an edict appointed Zong and Xu Ling as acting officials on a return embassy. Zong did not go because of illness. When Hou Jing raided the capital, an edict made Zong acting Minister of Ceremonies in charge of the lesser altars.
s0023.idiomatic: When friendship was restored with Wei, an edict appointed Zong and Xu Ling as acting officials on a return embassy. Zong did not go because of illness. When Hou Jing raided the capital, an edict made Zong acting minister of ceremonies in charge of the lesser altars.

s0024.literal: When the palace city fell, Zong fled in hardship over many years until he reached Kuaiji commandery and rested at Longhua Monastery, whereupon he composed the Cultivating the Mind rhapsody, briefly narrating the affairs of the time.
s0024.idiomatic: When the palace city fell, Zong fled in hardship over many years until he reached Kuaiji commandery and rested at Longhua Monastery, whereupon he composed the Cultivating the Mind rhapsody, briefly narrating the affairs of the time.

s0026.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the fourth year of Grand Clarity, I took refuge at Longhua Monastery in Kuaiji.
s0026.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn in the fourth year of Grand Clarity, I took refuge at Longhua Monastery in Kuaiji.

s0027.literal: This monastery was built in the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia by my sixth-generation ancestor, Song Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, Marquis of Zhouling.
s0027.idiomatic: This monastery was built in the twenty-fourth year of Yuanjia by my sixth-generation ancestor, Song's right vice director of the masters of writing and Marquis of Zhouling.

s0028.literal: The marquis's royal father's father was Jin Guardian General Jiang Biao, Editorial footnote marker 2. In former times he came to this commandery, chose a dwelling in Juyang ward of Shanyin, and bequeathed to his descendants the will to end their days here.
s0028.idiomatic: The marquis's great-grandfather served as Jin guardian general Jiang Biao; [2] in former times he came to this commandery, chose a dwelling in the Juyang ward of Shanyin, and left his descendants the wish to end their days here.

s0029.literal: The monastery grounds were the old site of the house; river to the left, lake to the right, mountains before and ravine behind; stretching east-west, winding north-south. For a time I shared daily life with monks of painful discipline; at dawn I kept precepts and read sutras, at evening I scanned books; I slept amid wind and cloud and dwelt leaning on water and moon.
s0029.idiomatic: The monastery grounds were the old site of the house: river to the left, lake to the right, mountains before and ravine behind, stretching east and west, winding north and south. For a time I shared daily life with monks of austere discipline; at dawn I kept precepts and read sutras, at evening I scanned books; I slept amid wind and cloud and dwelt leaning on water and moon.

s0030.literal: I did not expect that China and the barbarians could no longer be distinguished, that court and market had collapsed—on this I wound my feelings; the wounding, you may know.
s0030.idiomatic: I did not expect that China and the barbarians could no longer be distinguished, that court and market had collapsed—on this I wounded my feelings; the wounding, you may know.

s0031.literal: I suck tears and wet the brush—how could that vent what is knotted? I hope gentlemen born after who may pity this lot of mine.
s0031.idiomatic: I suck tears and wet the brush—how could that vent what is knotted? I hope gentlemen born after may pity this lot of mine.

s0032.literal: Favored by the asterism of the Southern Dipper, commencing the spirit-secrets of Eastern Yue; the cypress-wind praised in Han verse, Mount Zhen recorded in Zhou annals; holding Great Yu's metal books, engraved the (stone) characters of violent Qin, Editorial footnote marker 3. When the Grand Historian came to probe the crypt, Zhongli went away and opened the casket—truly bamboo and arrow-shafts are treasures; how could jade fragments be rare finds?
s0032.idiomatic: Favored by the asterism of the Southern Dipper, commencing the spirit-secrets of Eastern Yue; the cypress-wind praised in Han verse, Mount Zhen recorded in Zhou annals; holding Great Yu's metal books, engraved the (stone) records of violent Qin; [3] when the grand astrologer came to probe the crypt and Zhongli went away and opened the casket—truly bamboo and arrow-shafts are treasures; how could jade fragments be rare finds?

s0033.literal: I received the great virtue's soaring sacrifice and lodged in this old monastery of pacifying meditation—truly the old garden of Yuzhang, become a triumphant ground of yellow gold.
s0033.idiomatic: I received the great virtue's soaring sacrifice and lodged in this old monastery of pacifying meditation—truly the old garden of Yuzhang, become a triumphant ground of yellow gold.

s0034.literal: Then my silent, hidden heart, as in a mirror sought afar; I faced the towering former hill, near the deep, distant lake.
s0034.idiomatic: Then my silent, hidden heart, as in a mirror sought afar; I faced the towering former hill, near the deep, distant lake.

s0035.literal: Mountain branches lay sprawling; water leaves dripped and drenched; gibbons hung at dawn and fell away, hungry flying-squirrels cried by night.
s0035.idiomatic: Mountain branches lay sprawling; water leaves dripped and drenched; gibbons hung at dawn and fell away, hungry flying-squirrels cried by night.

s0036.literal: Fruit thickets and herb gardens, peach paths and orange groves—tips brushing cloud and sun, gloom knitting into shade.
s0036.idiomatic: Fruit thickets and herb gardens, peach paths and orange groves—tips brushing cloud and sun, gloom knitting into shade.

s0037.literal: I kept nature's elegant delight and scorned people's idle, tangled mess; I gazed at the winding islands and faced the heaped layers of the river's source; at night the drifting moon sailed far; at dawn trailing light and mist wound round.
s0037.idiomatic: I kept nature's elegant delight and scorned people's idle, tangled mess; I gazed at the winding islands and faced the heaped layers of the river's source; at night the drifting moon sailed far; at dawn trailing light and mist wound round.

s0038.literal: Wind drew cicadas to clamor and noise; rain drummed the groves and soughs through, Editorial footnote marker 4. Birds gradually grew tame and knew to come; clouds without feelings joined of themselves.
s0038.idiomatic: Wind drew cicadas to clamor and noise; rain drummed the groves in (soughing) sweep; [4] birds gradually grew tame and knew to come; clouds without feeling joined of themselves.

s0039.literal: Then the wilds opened to a spirit pagoda, the ground built for meditation dwelling; joy-garden stretched far, pleasure-trees stood sparse.
s0039.idiomatic: Then the wilds opened to a spirit pagoda, the ground built for meditation dwelling; joy-garden stretched far, pleasure-trees stood sparse.

s0040.literal: Walking the path over grass, feasting seated by the canal; holding precepts and shaking the staff, measuring shadow and eating humble greens—the grove of steadfastness could serve as parable, the field of quiet extinction for the moment seemed real.
s0040.idiomatic: Walking the path over grass, feasting seated by the canal; holding precepts and shaking the staff, measuring shadow and eating humble greens—the grove of steadfastness could serve as parable, the field of quiet extinction for the moment seemed real.

s0041.literal: Unlike the sadness rising when a tune ends, not like the sadness that begins when trees shed leaves—how could I lower my will and shame my body, or not show talent yet show myself?
s0041.idiomatic: Unlike the sadness rising when a tune ends, not like the sadness that begins when trees shed leaves—how could I lower my will and shame my body, or not show talent yet show myself?

s0042.literal: I tired of wind and rain as at darkened dusk, wearied of cockcrow clattering in my ears; blessed to flee the world and lodge on high, I relied on the surviving instructions of the charioteer who tunes the team.
s0042.idiomatic: I tired of wind and rain as at darkened dusk, wearied of cockcrow clattering in my ears; blessed to flee the world and lodge on high, I relied on the surviving instructions of the charioteer who tunes the team.

s0043.literal: I folded the subtle words of the four analyses and apprehended the wondrous principle of the three vehicles; I loosed the ten bindings of entanglement and brushed away the dust of five confusions; long I abandoned glory in power and profit, hoping to forget the ties of wife and children; I felt my spirit of former days and entrusted a knowing ear to future ages—why is the far traveler pitiable? I know how endless is self-pity.
s0043.idiomatic: I folded the subtle words of the four analyses and apprehended the wondrous principle of the three vehicles; I loosed the ten bindings of entanglement and brushed away the dust of five confusions; long I abandoned glory in power and profit, hoping to forget the ties of wife and children; I felt my spirit of former days and entrusted a knowing ear to future ages—why is the far traveler pitiable? I know how endless is self-pity.

s0044.literal: Zong's ninth uncle by marriage Xiao Bo had first seized Guangzhou; Zong again went from Kuaiji to rely on him.
s0044.idiomatic: Zong's ninth uncle by marriage Xiao Bo had first seized Guangzhou; Zong again went from Kuaiji to rely on him.

s0045.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang pacified Hou Jing, he summoned Zong as Resplendent Might General and interior governor of Shixing, granting eight hundred piculs of the commandery salary for Zong's travel expenses.
s0045.idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang pacified Hou Jing, he summoned Zong as resplendent might general and interior governor of Shixing, granting eight hundred piculs of the commandery salary for Zong's travel expenses.

s0046.literal: When Jiangling fell he could not go; from this Zong lodged in Lingnan for years on end.
s0046.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell he could not go; from this Zong lodged in Lingnan for years on end.

s0047.literal: In the fourth year of Tiancheng, he was summoned back to court as gentleman of the Secretariat; he attended at the Palace Secretariat.
s0047.idiomatic: In Tiancheng year 4 (565) he was summoned back to court as gentleman of the secretariat and attended at the palace secretariat.

s0048.literal: He rose in repeated promotions to right chief clerk of the Chamberlain's Office, keeper of eastern-palace records, attendant in the Yellow Gate handling affairs, and concurrently chief rectifier for southern Xuzhou.
s0048.idiomatic: He rose in repeated promotions to right chief clerk of the chamberlain's office, keeper of eastern-palace records, attendant in the yellow gate handling affairs, and concurrently chief rectifier for southern Xuzhou.

s0049.literal: Made junior mentor of the heir apparent and direct, clear-scattered-cavalry attendant; eastern-palace and rectifier posts as before.
s0049.idiomatic: He was made junior mentor of the heir apparent and direct, clear-scattered-cavalry attendant; his eastern-palace and rectifier posts remained as before.

s0050.literal: Promoted to Minister of the Masters of Writing for Households, transferred to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent; rectifier post as before.
s0050.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of the masters of writing for households and transferred to grand mentor of the heir apparent; his rectifier post remained as before.

s0051.literal: Because he drank with the heir through the night and reared the worthy concubine Lady Chen as his daughter, and the heir would slip out to Zong's quarters, the Emperor was angry and dismissed him.
s0051.idiomatic: Because he drank with the heir through the night and reared the worthy concubine Lady Chen as his daughter, and the heir would slip out to Zong's quarters, Emperor Xuan was angry and dismissed him.

s0052.literal: Soon he was made attendant and concurrently general of the left nimble cavalry.
s0052.idiomatic: Soon he was made attendant and concurrently general of the left nimble cavalry.

s0053.literal: Again Minister for Households and concurrently general of the left army; before he took the seal he was again dismissed on official business.
s0053.idiomatic: Again minister for households and concurrently general of the left army; before he took the seal he was again dismissed on official business.

s0054.literal: Soon he was raised as attendant of the scattered cavalry, resplendent lieutenant general, left chief clerk of the Chamberlain—and promoted to Minister of Ceremonies.
s0054.idiomatic: Soon he was raised as attendant of the scattered cavalry, resplendent lieutenant general, and left chief clerk of the chamberlain, then promoted to minister of ceremonies.

s0055.literal: Zong once narrated himself in summary, saying:
s0055.idiomatic: Zong once narrated himself in summary, saying:

s0056.literal: "Through repeated promotions I rose to clear distinction and filled every rank at court; I did not seek worldly profit or meddle with those in favor.
s0056.idiomatic: "Through repeated promotions I rose to clear distinction and filled every rank at court; I did not seek worldly profit or meddle with those in favor.

s0057.literal: Once I bent my body and sighed to heaven: Zhuang Qingdai rose to Chancellor yet left no trace that could be recorded;
s0057.idiomatic: Once I bent my body and sighed to heaven: Zhuang Qingdai rose to chancellor yet left no trace that could be recorded;

s0058.literal: Zhao Yuanshu was a memorial clerk to the throne and shines in the biographies.
s0058.idiomatic: Zhao Yuanshu was a memorial clerk to the throne and shines in the biographies.

s0059.literal: Since I took office in Chen I have never fawned on a single thing or intervened in a single affair.
s0059.idiomatic: Since I took office in Chen I have never fawned on a single thing or intervened in a single affair.

s0060.literal: Men adrift in the floating dust of the age quite bore me ill will; glory and ruin, favor and insult—I paid them no mind.
s0060.idiomatic: Men adrift in the floating dust of the age quite bore me ill will; glory and ruin, favor and insult—I paid them no mind.

s0061.literal: In the Taikian era authority shifted to petty men; flattery and jealousy played tyrant; I was repeatedly driven down—what can be done about fate?
s0061.idiomatic: In the Taikian era authority shifted to petty men; flattery and jealousy played tyrant; I was repeatedly driven down—what can be done about fate?

s0062.literal: In former days when Houzhu was in the eastern palace he took heed of literature and the arts; long I bore his clear favor, and our bond of grace was deep.
s0062.idiomatic: In former days when Houzhu was in the eastern palace he took heed of literature and the arts; long I bore his clear favor, and our bond of grace was deep.

s0063.literal: On the day he succeeded, for a time misplaced trust ran high; I took form in the heavenly storehouse and set right the myriad tasks; the eight standards and six canons—there was none I did not oversee.
s0063.idiomatic: On the day he succeeded, for a time misplaced trust ran high; I took form in the heavenly storehouse and set right the myriad tasks; the eight standards and six canons—there was none I did not oversee.

s0064.literal: In former days Emperor Wu of Jin, in his edict to Xun Gongzeng, said: 'The steward of Zhou is today's Director of the Masters of Writing.'
s0064.idiomatic: In former days Emperor Wu of Jin, in his edict to Xun Gongzeng, said: 'The steward of Zhou is today's director of the masters of writing.'

s0065.literal: How much more when my talent has not reached half the ancients', yet I hold the salary of a corpse?
s0065.idiomatic: How much more when my talent has not reached half the ancients', yet I hold the salary of a corpse?

s0066.literal: Jin Grand Guardian Lu Wan said, 'To make me one of the Three Dukes shows there is no man in the empire.'
s0066.idiomatic: Jin grand guardian Lu Wan said, 'To make me one of the three dukes shows there is no man in the empire.'

s0067.literal: Cap and chariot are things that may come by chance—how could they be what one must demand?
s0067.idiomatic: Cap and chariot are things that may come by chance—how could they be what one must demand?

s0068.literal: In my weak years I gave my heart to the Buddha's teaching; in my twenties I went to Zhongshan to receive the bodhisattva precepts from Master Ze of Lingyao Monastery.
s0068.idiomatic: In my weak years I gave my heart to the Buddha's teaching; in my twenties I went to Zhongshan to receive the bodhisattva precepts from Master Ze of Lingyao Monastery.

s0069.literal: In my declining years in office in Chen I kept close company with the cloth-robed superior of Mount She, deeply awakened to suffering's emptiness, and again practiced the precepts; I moved goodness in heart and walked compassion toward things, and knew somewhat how to urge myself—yet I could not live on vegetables alone and was still stained by dusty toil; on this account I bear shame all my life."
s0069.idiomatic: In my declining years in office in Chen I kept close company with the cloth-robed superior of Mount She, deeply awakened to suffering's emptiness, and again practiced the precepts; I moved goodness in heart and walked compassion toward things, and knew somewhat how to urge myself—yet I could not live on vegetables alone and was still stained by dusty toil; on this account I bear shame all my life."

s0070.literal: Zong's self-narration—men of the time called it a true record.
s0070.idiomatic: Zong's self-narration—men of the time called it a true record.

s0071.literal: Zong was earnest in conduct and righteousness, broad, harmonious, warm, and generous.
s0071.idiomatic: Zong was earnest in conduct and righteousness, broad, harmonious, warm, and generous.

s0072.literal: He loved learning and could compose prose; in five-word and seven-word verse he was especially skilled;
s0072.idiomatic: He loved learning and could compose prose; in five-word and seven-word verse he was especially skilled;

s0073.literal: yet he erred toward the florid and flashy, and so won Houzhu's favor and intimacy.
s0073.idiomatic: yet he erred toward the florid and flashy, and so won Houzhu's favor and intimacy.

s0074.literal: He had many private pieces; men who loved such things passed them along to recite and enjoy, and to this day they have not ceased.
s0074.idiomatic: He had many private pieces; men who loved such things passed them along to recite and enjoy, and to this day they have not ceased.

s0075.literal: In Houzhu's reign Zong held power like a chief minister yet did not take hold of government affairs; day after day he feasted with Houzhu in the rear court, together with Chen Xu, Kong Fan, Wang Chuo, Editorial footnote marker 5. and more than ten others—men of the time called them the intimate guests.
s0075.idiomatic: In Houzhu's reign Zong held power like a chief minister yet did not take hold of government affairs; day after day he feasted with Houzhu in the rear court, together with Chen Xu, Kong Fan, Wang Chuo, [5] and more than ten others—men of the time called them the intimate guests.

s0076.literal: From this state affairs daily declined, norms were not set; whoever spoke up was at once punished on a charge; ruler and ministers fell into darkness—until ruin.
s0076.idiomatic: From this state affairs daily declined, norms were not set; whoever spoke up was at once punished on a charge; ruler and ministers fell into darkness—until ruin.

s0077.literal: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls, which circulated in the world.
s0077.idiomatic: He had a collected works in thirty scrolls, which circulated in the world.

s0078.literal: His eldest son Yi, styled Shenyuan, had considerable literary gift.
s0078.idiomatic: His eldest son Yi, styled Shenyuan, had considerable literary gift.

s0079.literal: By nature he was arrogant and unbridled, relying on influence to bully others; even near kin and old friends did not escape his slander.
s0079.idiomatic: By nature he was arrogant and unbridled, relying on influence to bully others; even near kin and old friends did not escape his slander.

s0080.literal: His offices included associate in the Editorial Office, attendant of the heir apparent, groom, attendant in the Yellow Gate of the Secretariat, junior mentor of the heir apparent.
s0080.idiomatic: His offices included associate in the editorial office, attendant of the heir apparent, groom, attendant in the yellow gate of the secretariat, and junior mentor of the heir apparent.

s0081.literal: After entering Sui he was literary aide to the Prince of Qin.
s0081.idiomatic: After entering Sui he was literary aide to the Prince of Qin.

s0082.literal: His seventh son Cui was imperial son-in-law, secretary gentleman, Sui attendant handling affairs, and academician on direct duty at the Palace Secretariat.
s0082.idiomatic: His seventh son Cui was imperial son-in-law, secretary gentleman, Sui attendant handling affairs, and academician on direct duty at the palace secretariat.

s0083.literal: Yao Cha, styled Boshen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
s0083.idiomatic: Yao Cha, styled Boshen, came from Wukang in Wuxing commandery.

s0084.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Xin was Wu Grand Master of Ceremonies, famed on the left bank of the Yangzi.
s0084.idiomatic: His ninth-generation ancestor Xin was Wu's grand master of ceremonies, famed on the left bank of the Yangzi.

s0085.literal: As a child Cha had utmost nature; in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.
s0085.idiomatic: As a child Cha had an utmost nature; in serving his parents he was known for filial piety.

s0086.literal: At six he could recite more than ten thousand words of books.
s0086.idiomatic: At six he could recite more than ten thousand words of books.

s0087.literal: In youth he did not care for play; gambling and miscellaneous games never touched his mind.
s0087.idiomatic: In youth he did not care for play; gambling and miscellaneous games never touched his mind.

s0088.literal: With painful zeal he sharpened his spirit, continuing from night into day.
s0088.idiomatic: With painful zeal he sharpened his spirit, continuing from night into day.

s0089.literal: At twelve he could already compose literary pieces.
s0089.idiomatic: At twelve he could already compose literary pieces.

s0090.literal: His father, the Commissioner with the Upper Office, Sengyuan, Editorial footnote marker 6. was famed in the age of Liang's Emperor Wu; both palaces treated him with exceptional courtesy. Whenever he received provisions and gifts he would turn them to Cha and his brothers for travel-study funds; Cha used them all to gather and store books, and so his learning and sight grew daily broader.
s0090.idiomatic: His father, Commissioner Sengyuan, [6] was famed under Liang's Emperor Wu; both palaces treated him with exceptional courtesy. Whenever he received provisions and gifts he would turn them to Cha and his brothers for travel-study funds; Cha used them all to gather and store books, and so his learning and sight grew daily broader.

s0091.literal: At thirteen, when Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace and lavishly cultivated literary doctrine, Cha was at once brought into the Hall of Propagating Virtue to hear lectures and disputations, and Confucians praised him.
s0091.idiomatic: At thirteen, when Liang's Emperor Jianwen was in the eastern palace and lavishly cultivated literary doctrine, Cha was at once brought into the Hall of Propagating Virtue to hear lectures and disputations, and Confucians praised him.

s0092.literal: When Jianwen succeeded to the throne he showed Cha still more courtesy and reception.
s0092.idiomatic: When Jianwen succeeded to the throne he showed Cha still more courtesy and reception.

s0093.literal: He began his career as left regular attendant to the Prince of Nanhai and concurrently gentleman of the Secretariat for texts.
s0093.idiomatic: He began his career as left regular attendant to the Prince of Nanhai and concurrently gentleman of the secretariat for texts.

s0094.literal: Made acting aide in the Prince of Nanjun's establishment and concurrently gentleman of the Masters of Writing for the carriage-office.
s0094.idiomatic: He was made acting aide in the Prince of Nanjun's establishment and concurrently gentleman of the masters of writing for the carriage-office.

s0095.literal: When Liang's house fell into chaos he followed his two parents back to the home district from Jinling.
s0095.idiomatic: When Liang's house fell into chaos he followed his two parents back to the home district from Jinling.

s0096.literal: At the time the eastern lands suffered military famine; men starved and ate one another; there was nowhere to beg grain. Cha's household was numerous and all gathered wild plants to feed themselves.
s0096.idiomatic: At the time the eastern lands suffered military famine; men starved and ate one another; there was nowhere to beg grain. Cha's household was numerous and all gathered wild plants to feed themselves.

s0097.literal: Cha on every jagged hardship sought funds to support his parents, and grain constantly came in succession.
s0097.idiomatic: Cha on every jagged hardship sought funds to support his parents, and grain constantly came in succession.

s0098.literal: He also often took from his own share and pressed it on his younger brothers and sisters, even reaching old friends in want—he shared relief with them all; for himself he took only wild greens.
s0098.idiomatic: He also often took from his own share and pressed it on his younger brothers and sisters, even reaching old friends in want—he shared relief with them all; for himself he took only wild greens.

s0099.literal: Even amid chaos and separation he studied hard without ceasing.
s0099.idiomatic: Even amid chaos and separation he studied hard without ceasing.

s0100.literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang took the throne at Jingzhou, his father followed the court officials' example in going to the Western Terrace; Emperor Yuan appointed Cha magistrate of Yuanxiang.
